rule: A two-cell-thick multicoloured legend lies against one grid edge. The line touching the edge holds distinct keys, and the adjacent line holds their paired fill colours. Every 4-connected background component that does not reach the border and is bordered by exactly one colour is a hole. A hole whose bordering colour is a key is filled with that key's paired colour. Holes of non-key outlines, open outlines and pockets bordered by two colours stay unchanged.
scope: Random scenes: legend of 2..7 pairs on any of the four edges, at any valid offset; a 2x2 legend is never placed in a corner. Sides are mostly 4..20 and sometimes 21..30. The fixtures span 4..15, so larger sizes are a synthetic extension; bigger sprites (up to 9 cells, diamonds up to radius 4) are used when min side >= 16. Random scenes hold 1..8 objects: closed rectangles with ring-connected interior walls, chipped outlines, diamonds, optional pendant tails, non-key closed outlines (often a fill-only colour), open outlines (synthetic), and two-colour rings whose pocket stays empty (synthetic; only when the legend has >= 3 distinct colours). Sprites may interlock through their empty margins with a strict 8-neighbour gap. Explicit shapes reproduce the fixtures and accept an optional second outline colour. Not supported: touching or nested distinct objects, legends thicker than two cells, corner 2x2 legends (the reference reads these as vertical; this behaviour is deliberately not sampled), and non-zero backgrounds.

Legends are always exactly two cells thick and form one solid block.
Holes are always designed objects. Two-colour pockets appear only inside a single two-colour ring, never between two separately placed touching objects.
Rejection sampling is bounded at 400 scene attempts. Some constraint combinations that pass the up-front feasibility check can still fail with ValueError, for example num_shapes=8 on a small grid.
The up-front feasibility check runs only when both width and height are given, and it only tests room for one radius-1 diamond.
Explicit scenes skip the orientation-revealing check and the more-than-half-background check. They still require 0 to be the strictly most frequent colour.
Two-colour rings and open outlines are synthetic extensions that the fixtures do not demonstrate.
Sampled agreement and shape controls do not prove complete coverage of all valid scenes.

authored_constraints: Keys are distinct colours 1..9, and len(keys) == len(fills) in 2..9.
The legend is a solid 2 x k block touching its edge. Its key line is on the edge. The perpendicular grid size is >= 3, so the key side is uniquely nearer the edge.
A 2x2 legend is never in a corner. Its edge distance is 0 and its other-axis distance is >= 1, so the reference's horizontal/vertical tie-break agrees with the latent side.
Distinct objects and the legend never touch, even diagonally.
Each designed hole cell is 4-bordered only by its own object's outline or holes, and holes never touch the grid border.
The set of enclosed background cells equals the designed hole set exactly. There are no incidental pockets between objects, and open outlines genuinely leak.
Background 0 is strictly the most frequent colour. In random scenes it fills more than half the grid.
The legend has strictly more distinct colours than any other object. Two-colour objects require >= 3 distinct legend colours.
Every random sample changes at least one cell.

In every random sample, each wrong legend reading gives an output different from the true one: the swapped lines, and for 2x2 legends the two transposed readings. A legend for which some wrong reading always equals the truth is rejected or resampled.
When num_shapes >= 2 and a non-key colour exists, a random scene contains at least one closed non-key outline whose hole stays empty.
